report_name: Unit 42 Reveals 'Pass-ta-key' Attacks on Passwordless Systems

attack_patterns.name: Browser Information Discovery
attack_patterns.description: Malware enumerates passkey usage by reading Google Chrome's local sync database to build a target list of the victim's accounts.

attack_patterns.name: Credentials from Web Browsers
attack_patterns.description: The attack directly targets the LevelDB store in Google Chrome containing encrypted passkey material, which functions as a credential store.

attack_patterns.name: Steal Application Access Token
attack_patterns.description: By abusing the passkey authentication flow, the attacker effectively steals an access token in the form of a signed assertion to gain unauthorized access to the target service.

attack_patterns.name: Steal Web Session Cookie
attack_patterns.description: The attack achieves the goal of hijacking a user's authenticated session by forging the passkey authentication response, which is analogous to stealing a session cookie.

tools.name: Google Chrome
tools.description: The local data store used by Google Chrome to sync passkeys is targeted by malware to extract passkey metadata and private keys.

vulnerabilities.name: Passkey Synced Private Key Exposure
vulnerabilities.description: A weakness in Google's synced passkey implementation (Cloud Authenticator) that allows malware on a compromised endpoint to access and use passkey private keys from the local data store without user verification.

campaigns.name: Pass-ta-key Attacks
campaigns.description: A class of attacks targeting passwordless systems, specifically Google's synced passkey implementation, to silently authenticate, bypass user verification, and extract passkey private keys from a compromised endpoint.
campaigns.objective: Gain unauthorized access to accounts protected by passkeys.

identities.name: Google
identities.description: Vendor of the synced passkey ecosystem, including Google Chrome and the Cloud Authenticator, which was found to have weaknesses exploited by 'Pass-ta-key' attacks.

indicators.name: Suspicious Access to Chrome Passkey Store
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Access to Chrome Passkey Store
id: 2a1b4c3d-8e7f-4a9b-8c1d-2e3f4a5b6c7d
status: experimental
description: Detects processes other than chrome.exe accessing the Google Chrome LevelDB folder where synced passkey data is stored. This could indicate a 'Pass-ta-key' attack or other credential theft activity.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/passwordless-authentication-security-risks/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-03
tags:
  - attack.t1555.003
  - attack.credential_access
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
      - '\Sync Data\LevelDB\'
  filter:
    Image|endswith: '\chrome.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate backup software or other system utilities that might read these files.
level: medium
indicators.description: Detects processes other than chrome.exe accessing the Google Chrome LevelDB folder where synced passkey data is stored, a behavior associated with 'Pass-ta-key' attacks.
